title: DaVinci Resolve Remote Collaboration: Project Libraries, Shared Media, and Proxies
summary: Set up remote Resolve collaboration with a shared project library, accessible media, reliable proxies, and clear procedures for DRP handoffs and offline work.
body_markdown:
When you share a DaVinci Resolve project, the other editor receives its timelines, grades, and editing decisions, but still needs access to the footage, audio, graphics, and proxies it references. Without those files, the project can open with a timeline full of Media Offline clips.


Set up the shared project library and media access separately. The steps below use Blackmagic Cloud for the project and Aspect for the media, then cover sequential DRP handoffs and editing while offline.


## Separate the Resolve project from the media


Resolve keeps active projects in a **project library** . A project contains timelines, grades, and other project information, with references to media files. Blackmagic Cloud can host a shared library; a private DaVinci Resolve Project Server can support a team managing its own collaborative environment.


Media needs its own route to every workstation. That might be a local SSD, media synchronized through Blackmagic Cloud, or a mounted shared drive.[Blackmagic's collaboration documentation](https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/products/davinciresolve/collaboration) explicitly supports storage choices alongside its Cloud project workflow.


There's also a naming distinction when using Aspect. An Aspect project organizes shared assets and can appear as a mounted drive. A Resolve project holds the edit. Giving someone access to one does not automatically give them access to the other.


The edit project and the media library appear as separate resources, each with its own access key. What the team shares Where it belongs What to verify


Active Resolve project Cloud project library or a supported private Project Server Both editors can open the intended project and use its collaboration controls.


Originals, audio, graphics, and proxies Local copies, synchronized storage, or a mounted shared drive Each workstation can open the files referenced by the project.


Exported cuts and feedback A review service or agreed review location Everyone is discussing the correct revision.


An exported` .drp` belongs in a handoff or backup process. It's a snapshot of a Resolve project, and it does not include the source media or keep updating as the edit changes.


## Choose how the team will share editing decisions


If your editors need to work at the same time, start with Blackmagic Cloud or a private Project Server. Blackmagic Cloud avoids making your facility responsible for hosting the project server. A private server can suit a team that needs control over its own network environment and has someone responsible for connectivity and administration.


Resolve's collaboration controls include locking and update handling so collaborators can work without simply overwriting each other's changes. Assign work areas clearly: one editor can build interview selects while another assembles a different timeline. When both need the same work area, coordinate the change and use Resolve's update and comparison tools.


If work moves from one person to the next, sequential DRP handoffs may be sufficient. Keep active local project libraries on the individual workstations, export a new DRP for each handoff, and record who owns the next edit. Putting a local library or a DRP on a synchronized drive isn't a substitute for configuring Resolve collaboration.


## Decide whether editors will download or stream the media


### Local copies


Local copies suit a small team with enough SSD capacity, a stable media package, or long periods without connectivity. Each editor receives the required originals or proxies before work starts. Someone must also distribute newly added media and keep the folder structure consistent.


Once the copies arrive, editors can play them without depending on the internet connection. Keep a file inventory and send new media to every editor as it's added to the project.


### Blackmagic Cloud media synchronization


Blackmagic Cloud can synchronize media between collaborators so each has local files. Its workflow also supports proxies and Blackmagic Proxy Generator, which watches nominated folders and generates proxy files from new camera originals.


Editors who already use Blackmagic Cloud for their projects can use its media synchronization to receive local copies through the same service. Plan the required local storage and transfer time separately from the project library. Sharing a lightweight project doesn't mean the camera originals have finished arriving.


### Mounted media through Aspect


With[Aspect's mounted media access](https://aspect.inc/features/instant-access) , the project appears as a drive and applications request the file data they need. Editors can browse the shared folder structure without first downloading the whole project. Playback still depends on the connection, the number of streams, the codec, and the workstation's decoding capacity.


Shared media can be accessible while playback is still constrained by the connection and workstation. When the assistant adds footage to Aspect, the editors can access it from the same mounted project. Pin the files needed for a session or use lighter proxies on slower connections. The[Aspect desktop app](https://aspect.inc/docs/apps/desktop) supports macOS and Windows.

## Set up two remote editors against the same media


For example, Maya and Theo are editing a 90-second film called Harbor. Maya builds the interview sequence while Theo prepares supporting footage. They use a shared Resolve project in Blackmagic Cloud and an Aspect project for the media.


### 1. Agree on the working environment


Use the same Resolve version across the team and agree on project settings before building timelines. Check the fonts, plug-ins, graphics, and other dependencies the edit requires. A shared media folder can't supply a missing installed plug-in.


Choose who manages the main timeline, who imports new media, and who prepares proxies. These assignments reduce conflicting changes and duplicate processing without preventing collaborators from working at the same time.


### 2. Give both editors project and media access


In Resolve's Project Manager, sign in to Blackmagic Cloud and create a library dedicated to Harbor. Open the library's **Details** controls, choose **Share** , and enter the second editor's Blackmagic ID. The[Resolve 21.1 manual](https://documents.blackmagicdesign.com/UserManuals/DaVinci_Resolve_21.1_Reference_Manual.pdf?_v=1788850811000) states that shared library members can modify and delete any project within that library, which is why unrelated client projects should stay elsewhere.


Create or import the Resolve project into that library, open it, and choose **File > Multiple User Collaboration** . Both editors should work in this shared project.


Separately, give both editors access to the Harbor project in Aspect. Aspect's[sharing and permissions guide](https://aspect.inc/docs/share-and-present/sharing-and-permissions) distinguishes workspace access from project roles. For example, a freelance editor can be a Limited Member with Editor access to the production they're working on. Confirm both editors can open the Resolve project and read the media before assigning work.


### 3. Establish a stable media root


Upload the originals, production audio, and graphics into the Aspect project, then[mount that project](https://aspect.inc/docs/instant-access/mount-a-project) through the desktop app on both computers. Keep the project name, folder structure, and source filenames stable.


Use a consistent media root, such as` /Volumes/Harbor` on Macs or the same assigned drive letter on Windows, with camera footage and audio in clearly named folders. In Resolve's Media page, import from that mounted root. If it's absent from the Media Storage browser, add the location under **Preferences > System > Media Storage** .


When storage roots differ, use **Project Settings > Path Mapping** to associate the shared media location with each workstation's local path, or relink to the correct media location. Preserve the folder hierarchy and check several clips afterward, including shots from different camera cards. Repeated camera filenames make a visual check more useful than merely confirming that the red offline indicators disappeared.


### 4. Create and validate editing proxies


Choose proxy format and resolution in Resolve's Project Settings, select the source clips in the Media Pool, and use **Generate Proxy Media** . Put shared proxies in the mounted production project and wait for them to synchronize before the second editor relies on them.


Aspect also offers **Copy videos as proxies** , which copies generated MP4 proxies while keeping the originals. Use **Link Proxy Media** in Resolve to attach the corresponding files. For externally generated proxies, Resolve requires the same filename except for its extension, identical timecode and frame rate, and a supported format and codec. Also verify duration, picture alignment, and audio layout. Generate a replacement in Resolve if a copied proxy does not match.


Set **Playback > Proxy Handling > Prefer Proxies** for the edit. Check an interview clip, a long take, and any multichannel audio on both machines. Scrub to the beginning and end of each clip and switch between proxy and original playback to catch alignment or audio differences.


### 5. Keep generated caches local and verify collaboration


Set Resolve's cache location to a fast local SSD. Resolve's render cache and[Aspect's media cache](https://aspect.inc/docs/instant-access/manage-cache) serve different purposes: one holds generated processing results, while the other retains media data streamed from storage.


Have Maya make a small, recognizable change in her assigned timeline and confirm that Theo receives it through Resolve's collaboration workflow. Then check a newly added media file on both workstations. This verifies project updates and media availability independently before the full edit depends on them.


## Name an owner for every DRP handoff


For a sequential workflow, the outgoing editor saves the project, opens Project Manager, and chooses **Export Project** . Use **Export Project With Stills and LUTs** when the handoff needs those grading resources. Save the DRP into the shared handoff folder with a clear name, such as` Harbor_Edit_2026-09-28_v03.drp` , and wait for synchronization to finish.


The receiving editor imports that DRP into their own project library, opens it, and confirms that its timelines find the expected media. Record the version, the next editor, the intended timeline, and any missing dependencies in the handoff note. The receiving editor exports a new DRP when the next handoff is ready.


If two people continue editing separate imports, they have created two branches of the work. Appoint someone to compare and integrate those changes deliberately. A newer filename or completed file synchronization does not decide which creative changes should enter the master project.


A copied project can split into separate edit branches that need deliberate reconciliation.


## Prepare offline work as a separate project session


Before you go offline, export a DRP from the Cloud project and import it into a local project library. Agree on the scope of that session and how the results will return to the shared project. For example, Theo might work on a new selects timeline while Maya continues the main edit online.


Pin the actual proxies, audio, graphics, and other files that local project references. Pin originals as well if the session requires grading or full-quality output. Wait until pinning finishes, leave enough SSD space for working files, and check the intended timeline without the network before departing.


After reconnecting, synchronize new media and the exported handoff, then have the designated editor integrate the agreed work into the shared Resolve project. Media synchronization and Resolve project integration remain separate steps.


## Review the correct cut and finish from the intended sources


Give reviewers an exported cut with an identifiable revision. Blackmagic Cloud Presentations provides a review workflow connected to Resolve; Aspect can also hold review exports with[comments tied to each version](https://aspect.inc/docs/review-and-approve/versioning) . Choose the review destination before sending the first cut and keep client notes there, so editors do not have to reconcile feedback across several services.


Before finishing, choose **Playback > Proxy Handling > Disable All Proxies** and confirm that the required originals are available. **Prefer Camera Originals** can fall back to proxies when an original is missing, so disabling proxies makes that problem visible before delivery. Inspect picture, audio, and effects, and pin demanding media ahead of a grading session when the connection cannot sustain playback. For a master from originals, leave **Use proxy media** off in the Deliver page's advanced video settings and check any settings that reuse optimized media or render caches.


Keep the delivered cut with its approval record and a DRP export of the final Resolve project. Include the source media location and any fonts, plug-ins, or grading resources in the handoff notes so another editor can reopen the work for a later revision.


## FAQ


A Cloud project library holds the Resolve project, including its timelines and editing decisions. Each collaborator still needs access to the files that project references. Blackmagic Cloud media synchronization is one option; local media copies and supported shared storage are other options. Check project access and media access separately during setup.


A DRP is an exported snapshot that must be imported into a Resolve project library. It does not update as someone continues editing, and synchronizing it does not create Resolve's live collaboration controls. Use a shared Cloud or server-based project for simultaneous work, or give one editor ownership of each sequential DRP handoff.


Yes. Aspect keeps media on a mounted project drive while Blackmagic Cloud manages the shared Resolve project. Each editor needs access to both services and a media path that resolves correctly on their workstation. Keep Resolve's generated cache local and choose proxies or fully pinned media when the session needs them.


No. Resolve requires externally generated proxies to match the source filename except for its extension, timecode, and frame rate, and to use a supported format and codec. Also verify duration, picture alignment, and audio layout. Attach Aspect's MP4 proxy copies to the matching originals in Resolve and check picture and sound before editing. Generate proxies from the originals in Resolve if the copied files do not match.


Pinning makes complete files available locally once their downloads finish. It does not merge Resolve project changes. Before going offline, export a DRP, import it into a local project library, pin the referenced media, and agree who will integrate the resulting work after reconnection. Pinning the DRP alone does not pin its footage.


The project can be accessible even when its referenced files are unavailable on that workstation. Check that the media drive is mounted, the user has access, the files have finished transferring, and the paths match. Resolve's path mapping or relinking tools can address location differences. Open clips from each camera card afterward and check their picture and sound, especially when filenames repeat.
